content: Mallinckrodt Incorporated is a company that supplies pharmaceuticals, chemicals, imaging products, and respiratory equipment. It is based in the St. Louis, Missouri area and was recently acquired by Tyco Healthcare, a division of Tyco International. Following the acquisition, there have been proposals for further reorganization of the company. One division of Mallinckrodt, known as Mallinckrodt Baker, was formed through a merger with a chemical supplier originally founded by John Townshend Baker. This division holds a license to import coca leaves. Due to federal restrictions, the importation of drugs derived from cocaine, such as Esterom, is prohibited. As a result, manufacturers of such drugs are required to source their coca leaves from this licensed supplier. Additionally, Mallinckrodt has been involved in the importation of opium from India. The company was led in the 1940s by an individual who played a significant role in its operations during that time. A notable legal precedent involving Mallinckrodt, Inc. was established in the case Mallinckrodt, Inc. v. Medipart, Inc., 976 F.2d 700, 708 (Fed. Cir. 1992). This decision affirmed the right of patent holders to impose restrictions on the use of their products even after the point of sale. This ruling was later referenced in the case Arizona Cartridge Remanufacturers Association, Inc. v. Lexmark International, Inc., which upheld the enforceability of end-user licensing agreements, such as those found on software packaging, against customers.
